CMRCs exhibit a slow-wave effect, which enables physical shortening of longitudinal circuit dimensions while retaining (within a certain frequency range) approximate electrical or wave parameters. The primary challenge in design of CMRC-based devices is proper adjustment of independent variables. Due to typically intricate CMRC geometries described by a large number of wide-ranged parameters (as compared to ordinary TLs), finding a reasonable starting point for subsequent design optimization poses considerable difficulties. Here, a novel algorithm for reliable CMRC optimization is proposed, which utilizes a combination of pattern search procedures, response features, and variable-fidelity EM simulations. As demonstrated through comprehensive case studies, the algorithm is capable of converging to a good solution regardless of the initial design. Furthermore, the CMRC optimizer is embedded in the design framework, which permits determining a minimum-size coupler with electrical performance that still satisfies design requirements imposed on the structure.

Author Keywords: EM optimization, EM-driven design, feature-based optimization, pattern search, rat-race couplers, variable-fidelity EM models.

articleTitle: The Effect of Pitch Circle Diameter of Electrodes on Current Distributions in Submerged Arc Furnace
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: This work presents computations of electric current distributions inside an industrial submerged arc furnace. A 3D model has been developed in ANSYS Fluent that solves Maxwell's equations based on scalar and vector potential approach that are treated as transport equations. In this paper, the approach is described in detail and numerical simulations are performed on an industrial three-phase submerged arc furnace. The current distributions within electrodes due to a change in pitch circle diameter of electrodes are presented. The results show that proximity effect decreases as the electrodes apart further.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Frequency Variation Models of Quad-Ridge Flared Horn Reflector Feed Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Comparisons between several adaptive sampling and modeling schemes are presented to model the input impedance as well as radiation patterns of a quad-ridge flared horn antenna. This class of antennas operate over wide bandwidths as reflector feeds, and an accurate model of the radiation pattern over frequency is required during the design and analysis phase. It is shown that rational function interpolation, with adaptive frequency sampling trained purely on the input impedance, can provide rapidly converging models, which are straightforward to implement.

articleTitle: Acceleration techniques for semiclassical Maxwell-Bloch systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: The Maxwell-Bloch algorithm for simulating semiclassical quantum systems (such as interacting quantum dots) scales poorly for large numbers of particles due to an inherent computational complexity in the propagation calculation. Unfortunately, readily available methods that accelerate this calculation fail underneath a rotating-wave framework. The plane-wave timedomain algorithm, for instance, offers no performance benefit at time steps corresponding the bandwidth in a rotating (i.e. downshifted) frame. To overcome this we present an efficient alternative based on Adaptive Integral Method (AIM) that optimizes for any linear space-time differential operator acting on a potential function. We include results demonstrating the efficiency of this approach and its use in Maxwell-Bloch systems.

articleTitle: Multifidelity Modeling of Ultrasonic Testing Simulations with Cokriging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Multifidelity methods are introduced to the nondestructive evaluation (NDE) of measurement systems. In particular, Cokriging interpolation metamodels of physics-based ultrasonic testing (UT) simulation responses are utilized to accelerate the uncertainty propagation in model-assisted NDE. The proposed approach is applied to a benchmark test case of UT simulations and compared with the current state-of-the-art techniques. The results show that Cokriging captures the physics of the problem well and is able to reduce the computational burden by over one order of magnitude compared to the state of the art. To the best of the author's knowledge, this the first time multifidelity methods are applied to model-assisted NDE problems.

articleTitle: Dispersion Characteristics of Symmetrical/Asymmetrical Coupled Microstrip Type Structures with Stratified Anisotropic Media
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: This paper presents an extension of modal Galerkin's technique based on the recurrence process for determining the dispersion characteristics of multilayered coupled microstriptype structures consisting of stratified uniaxial anisotropic media. For this purpose, formalism concept of mathematical operators is introduced to more easily determine the impedance operator which constitutes an important element in the resolution of boundary conditions. By properly choosing trial functions appearing through this integral technique, appropriate numerical results are obtained and compared to those available in the literature to confirm efficiency and accuracy of this approach.

articleTitle: Surrogate-Assisted Tolerance Analysis of Microstrip Linear Arrays with Corporate Feeds
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: The paper addresses the problem of fast statistical analysis of linear array antennas with corporate feeds using surrogate-assisted methods. Realistic design has to take into account manufacturing tolerances that normally lead to a degradation of array performance with respect to both electrical and field parameters. Tolerances may be pertinent to antenna elements, element spacing, geometry parameters of the corporate feed, as well as material parameters of the substrate. The main performance figure affected by these parameter deviations is the sidelobe level (SLL). Accurate evaluation of SLL requires full-wave EM analysis of the array which is very expensive in computational terms. Consequently, performing statistical analysis directly at the level EM array model is impractical. Here, we discuss simple techniques that permit speeding up the process. These include various surrogate modeling methods as well as correction techniques that are used to align the fast surrogates with the respective EM models.

articleTitle: Ab-initio simulation of single carbon-cluster electron device
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: A non-symmetrical C100 Fullerene molecule enclosed by three electrodes (source, drain, gate) made of gold has been chosen as the test configuration for single electron device (SET). Quantum transport of single electrons, under direct control of external electrodes has been rigorously simulated by density functional theory (DFT). The importance and the potential of the above device include operation at low power, and uniquely high charge sensitivity due to Coulomb blockade, possibly observable up to the room temperature.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Design of Compact Microwave Components with Data-Driven Surrogates and Pareto Front Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: The paper discusses low-cost multi-objective optimization of compact microwave components using variablefidelity EM simulation models and data-driven surrogates. Our approach builds upon a recently reported method where the initial approximation of the Pareto set is obtained by optimizing the kriging surrogate constructed from sampled data of the coarsediscretization EM model of the structure at hand, with selected designs further refined to obtain the high-fidelity Pareto set. The drawback of the method is a large number of training data samples required to set up the surrogate. Here, considerable savings concerning the training data set size are achieved by Pareto front decomposition based on auxiliary points identified along the front and setting up the kriging models in the corresponding subdomains. The key factor is that the total volume of the sub-domains is considerably smaller than the volume of the original domain. Our considerations are illustrated using a compact rat-race coupler with design optimization cost savings of 29- and 30-percent for two and three sub-domains, respectively.

articleTitle: Direct Solution of General H2-Matrix with Controlled Accuracy and Change of Cluster Bases for Large-Scale Electromagnetic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Both dense and sparse matrices resulting from an electromagnetic analysis, in general, can be represented as an H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> matrix in controlled accuracy. In this paper, we develop a new direct solution of a general H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> -matrix. The new solution possesses not only explicitly controlled accuracy, but also a change of cluster basis to efficiently account for the updates to the original matrix during the direct solution procedure. Comparisons with state-of-the-art direct solutions have demonstrated a much reduced CPU run time of the new solution, in addition to a significantly improved accuracy, which is also controllable. Rapid and accurate direct solutions of millions of unknowns have been obtained on a single CPU core.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide with Tapered Electromagnetic Bandgap Structures for Bandpass Filter Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: A planar filter is proposed, designed, and implemented through a structure of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and half mode SIW with Tapered Electromagnetic Bandgap structure (TEBG). These bandpass filters are designed using many tapering windows. Through the appropriate design three rows of tapered periodic structures, which are characterized by different central frequency of the passband are used. Numerical simulations show a satisfactory agreement with experiments. The proposed SIW filter is a promising element for the design of high-performance telecommunication systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of Waveguide Extracted Poles
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: A fast and accurate modal method for analysing waveguide extracted poles of microwave filters is presented. Basing on a previously presented analysis of a six-port junction in rectangular waveguide [1], by properly shorting the unused ports and reducing the upward directed port the required slot coupling is achieved. Additionally, the case of two contiguous extracted poles is also considered. A parallel FEM analysis of the structures confirms the accuracy of the proposed analysis method.

articleTitle: An Efficient EM-based Ultra-Wideband Bandpass Filter Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient full wave electromagnetic (EM) design and optimization method for ultra-wideband bandpass filter is proposed. An ultra-wideband bandpass filter with 100% fractional bandwidth is designed using Sonnet EM simulator to verify the proposed method. The proposed method follows a sequential optimization process where a group of single terminated sub-networks are established by successively adding, extracting and optimizing design parameters, by using this segmented design method, only a few couplings and resonators are designed and optimized in each design stage, which improve the convergence of the whole process. Moreover, the frequency dependent couplings which are not covered in conventional coupling matrix model are well characterized by extracting the input impedance of the single terminated sub-network over the ultra-wide frequency range of interest from the reflected group delay response. The space mapping technique is employed to improve the EM based optimization process. By using the method, excellent agreement between the EM response and the design specification is obtained in the ultra-wideband bandpass filter design example.

articleTitle: Novel Multi-mode Wideband Filters based on Cone Half-mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this paper a novel dual-mode and triple-mode wideband filters using cone half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) resonator are proposed. To design the two filters a metallic perturbation via is introduced in two different positions in the structure. Taking the advantage of the cavity form, the resonant frequencies can be controlling with the metallic via position. To define the optimized via location in the both filters, the resonant frequencies of the perturbed cavity are analyzed first by eigen-mode HFSS simulator. Finally the first two resonant modes are utilized to form the dual-mode filter and the second, the third and the fourth resonant modes are utilized to design the triple-mode filter. Two higher-order filters that use two dual-mode or triple-mode cavities were also proposed.
